transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. What brings you here today?

Um… I guess the thing that finally made me come in is I’m not really eating like I used to. Like, it’s gotten to where I’ll be at work, on my lunch break at the store, and I’ll buy something I normally like—stuff I used to actually look forward to—and then I just kind of sit there staring at it. I’ll take maybe a couple bites, or sometimes not even that, and then I end up throwing most of it away.

It feels stupid saying that out loud, because it’s just lunch, you know, but it’s been bothering me. I work retail, so lunch break is kind of one of the only times in the day where I’m supposed to just sit down and eat, and lately I just… don’t want it. The food doesn’t seem appealing, even when I know I should be hungry. That’s what made me think maybe I should ask for help, because it doesn’t feel normal for me.
Have you noticed yourself feeling down or losing interest in things you used to enjoy, like hobbies or spending time with friends?

Yeah… yeah, I think that’s actually been happening a lot. It’s not even like I’m always sitting there crying or something, it’s more like everything that used to make me feel like myself just feels kind of… flat now.

Like, I used to get really excited about gallery nights around town. I’d hear about one and plan around it, even if I was tired from work, because I liked seeing what people made and just being around that whole thing. And basketball too—I used to like playing, even just casually, not like I was amazing or anything, but it felt good to run around and joke with people. Lately if someone mentions going, I’ll say I’m busy or I’m too tired, but honestly I just don’t feel that pull to go.

Same with little stuff, like getting food-truck tacos with people. That used to be something I’d actually look forward to, standing around, talking, trying different places. Now I’ll go sometimes and just kind of stand there feeling like I’m not really in it, and then I’m looking for a reason to leave early.

And there’s this art stuff I used to help with for kids sometimes, and I liked that a lot before. It made me feel useful, I guess. But lately even that feels hard to care about. I’ll show up and be there physically, but inside it’s like nothing really lands. I hate saying that because it makes me sound cold, and I don’t want to be that way. I just… don’t feel the same interest in things anymore.
Have you noticed feeling down or having a low mood most of the time, even outside of work or when you’re alone?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that. I mean… I don’t know if I’d call it “down” all the time exactly. It’s more like I feel kind of muted, if that makes sense? Like I can get through the day and talk to customers and do what I’m supposed to do, and then when I’m by myself it’s not always like I’m actively sad, it’s just… I don’t feel like much is there.

Sometimes I’ll notice it more when I’m sitting at home and there’s nothing distracting me, but I don’t know if that counts as low mood or just being tired. I guess I haven’t really been keeping track of it in that way. It’s not like I wake up every morning and think, “I’m depressed,” or anything. It’s more that things feel heavier than they used to, but I’m not sure how much of the time that’s happening.
Have you found yourself feeling like you're not good enough or blaming yourself for things more than usual?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t know if I would’ve described it that way before, but lately I keep getting stuck on this idea that I’m not really good enough for things people are saying I’m good enough for.

Like at work, there was this award thing, and people acted like I earned it, and I know on paper I guess I did the job or whatever, but I keep thinking… no, they must not be seeing it right. Like I don’t deserve it. And then there’s been talk about maybe giving me a chance at supervisor, and instead of feeling proud or excited, I mostly feel this guilt in my stomach, like I somehow tricked everyone into thinking I’m better than I am.

People tell me, “No, you didn’t trick anybody, you work hard,” and I try to hear that, but it doesn’t really stick. I just keep replaying it and thinking they’re going to realize they made a mistake. And then I feel bad for even being considered, like someone else should have gotten it and I’m taking up space I didn’t earn. It’s embarrassing, because I know it probably sounds like I’m fishing for reassurance, but it doesn’t feel like that. It feels like I actually did something wrong, even though I can’t point to what.
Have you noticed that you feel more tired than usual, even if you haven’t been doing much, or that you don’t have the same energy to get through the day as you used to?

Yeah… yeah, I have noticed that. It’s kind of embarrassing because it doesn’t always match what I’m actually doing. Like I’ll be at work, and the first part of the shift I can usually make myself move around and act normal enough, but by the middle of it my body starts feeling really heavy.

Even little things start feeling like they take way more out of me than they should. Straightening the racks, walking back to the stockroom, going to grab something for a customer… stuff I’ve done a million times without even thinking about it. Lately it’s like my legs don’t want to cooperate, or like I’m carrying extra weight around. Not pain exactly, just this drained feeling.

And I’ll catch myself standing there for a second before I go do something, not because I’m trying to be lazy, but because it feels like I have to talk myself into moving. I don’t like that. I used to be able to get through a shift and still feel like I had something left in me, but now halfway through I’m already thinking, “How am I going to get through the rest of this?”
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep lately, like having trouble falling asleep, waking up frequently during the night, or sleeping much more or much less than usual?

Yeah… sleep has been kind of messed up, I guess. Not like I’m up all night every single night, but most nights I get in bed and then my brain just starts going. It’s like the second there’s nothing else happening, I start replaying stuff from the store.

Especially the award thing. I’ll go back over what people said, how they looked when they said it, whether they really meant it, whether they were just being nice, whether I looked stupid accepting it… and then I start thinking about the supervisor conversations too, like if they’re talking about me when I’m not there, or if they’re going to realize they picked the wrong person. It just keeps looping, and I’ll tell myself, “Just stop thinking about it,” but that doesn’t really do anything.

Sometimes I do eventually fall asleep, but then I’ll wake up way too early, like before I need to be up, and once I’m awake my mind turns right back on. I can’t get it to shut back off. I’ll just lie there staring at the ceiling or checking the time and thinking, “If I fall asleep right now I can still get a little more,” but then that makes me more awake somehow. So yeah, it’s definitely not normal for me lately.
Have you noticed that your thoughts feel slower than usual, or that it's harder to focus or make decisions, even about small things?

Yeah… I think that’s been happening, actually. I didn’t really connect it to anything at first, because it sounds so small, but at work I keep losing my place on things that should be easy for me.

Like if I’m counting inventory, I’ll get halfway through a shelf or a box and then suddenly I’m not sure what number I was on, so I have to start over. And then I start getting annoyed with myself because it’s not complicated math or anything, it’s just counting, but my brain feels like it slips off the track. I’ll be standing there staring at the items, trying to remember if I counted that row already, and then I second-guess it so much that I don’t trust whatever number I came up with.

Same with setting up displays. Picking colors or deciding what should go where used to be something I could do pretty fast. I mean, maybe not perfect, but I could just make a choice and move on. Now I’ll stand there with two shirts or whatever and go back and forth like it’s some huge decision. I’ll think, “This one looks better,” and then immediately think, “No, that’s wrong, why would you pick that?” And then I waste time on it and feel stupid because it’s such a basic part of my job.

So yeah, I don’t know if my thoughts are slower exactly, but it feels harder to stay focused and harder to trust little decisions I used to make without thinking so much.
Have you ever felt like life isn’t worth living, or had thoughts about not wanting to be alive?

I… I don’t know. I mean, I don’t think I’ve had it in the way you’re asking, like where I’ve sat down and thought, “I don’t want to be alive,” or anything clear like that.

Sometimes I do get really worn down and I’ll think things like, “I can’t keep feeling like this,” but that feels more like being overwhelmed than actually wanting to die. I don’t know if that makes sense. It’s more like I want everything to stop for a while, or I want my head to quiet down, not that I’ve made some decision or plan or something.

So… no, I don’t think I’ve had thoughts about not wanting to be alive. Not really.
Would you say that you’ve been feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, not just occasionally or in response to specific things?

I’m not really sure how to answer that cleanly. I mean, I wouldn’t say I’m happy or anything, but “depressed most of the day nearly every day” sounds… I don’t know, like a very specific thing, and I don’t know if I can say that for sure.

There are definitely parts of the day where I feel really low or heavy, but sometimes it feels more tied to whatever I’m thinking about at that moment, or what’s happening around me. Like if I’m busy, I might not notice it as much, and then when things get quiet it kind of comes back. So I don’t know if that counts as most of the day or not.

I guess I’ve felt off for a while, but I’m not sure I’d describe it as being down all day, every day. It’s more like it comes in waves, or it’s sitting in the background and gets louder sometimes. Does that make sense?
How long have you been feeling this way overall — like things feel flat, you don’t have the same interest in activities, and everything feels heavier than before?

I think… overall it’s been about two months. Maybe a little hard to pin down exactly, because at first I didn’t think of it like “something started,” you know? It just felt like I was tired or stressed or maybe I was overthinking things.

But if I’m being honest, it lines up pretty close with when I got that window display award at work, and then the district manager started paying attention to me. Everyone was making a big deal about it for a while, and after that is when things started feeling different. Like the stuff that used to feel normal or even kind of enjoyable started feeling heavier, flatter, like I had to force myself through it more.

So… yeah. I’d say around two months, since all that attention happened after the display award.
Have you noticed that you no longer get any pleasure or satisfaction out of things you used to enjoy, like the art events or playing basketball?

Yeah… yeah, I have noticed that. I mean, I didn’t really want to call it that at first, because it sounds dramatic, like I suddenly hate everything, and it’s not exactly that. It’s more like I’ll go through the motions and I know, in my head, that I used to like it, but I’m not really feeling anything from it.

Like gallery nights, those used to be something I’d actually look forward to. I’d think about what I wanted to see, or who might be there, or I’d get ideas for my own stuff. Now if I go, I kind of just stand around looking at the walls, and everyone else seems into it, and I’m just… flat. Like I’m there but not really there. Same with basketball. I used to like playing, even just messing around, getting some energy out. Lately I’ll show up and after a few minutes I’m already thinking of some excuse to leave.

Even little stuff, like grabbing tacos from the food trucks, that used to feel like a treat, you know? Or helping kids with art things, that used to make me feel useful. Now I’ll do it and I’m just waiting for it to be over. Then I feel bad because those are things I’m supposed to enjoy, or I used to enjoy them, and I can’t really explain why they don’t hit the same.

So, yeah… I guess I don’t get much pleasure or satisfaction from those things lately. I usually just make some excuse and leave early if I can.
Would you say that you've experienced a loss of energy or feel fatigued nearly every day, even when you haven’t been doing much?

Yeah… I think so. I didn’t really notice it at first because I kept telling myself, like, everybody gets tired at work, you know? Retail is standing around, moving stuff, dealing with people, going back and forth, so I thought maybe it was just normal.

But it feels different lately. By the middle of a shift my body starts feeling really heavy, like I’m wearing wet clothes or something. Even little things that shouldn’t be a big deal — straightening racks, folding things again, walking to the stockroom to grab something — it takes more out of me than it should. I’ll catch myself sort of standing there for a second before doing it, like I have to talk myself into moving.

And it’s not always after I’ve done some huge amount of work either. Sometimes the shift hasn’t even been that busy, and I still feel drained like I’ve already worked the whole day. I don’t know if I’d say I’m collapsing or anything, but yeah, it’s there a lot. Most days at work, especially halfway through, I feel worn down in a way that doesn’t really match what I’ve actually been doing.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently, like a significant decrease or increase in how much you eat or how much you weigh?

Yeah… that’s actually one of the main things that made me think I should maybe ask for help, because I barely want to eat anymore.

Like, I’ll be on my lunch break at the store, and I’ll get something I used to like — something easy, nothing weird — and I’ll just sit there staring at it. I’ll take a few bites maybe, but it feels like I’m eating because I know I’m supposed to, not because I want it. And then most of it ends up in the trash. I’ll look at it like, “Why did I even buy this?” but then if I don’t buy anything, I also feel like I’m being stupid because I know I should eat during a shift.

It’s not like I’m trying to diet or anything. Food just doesn’t really seem appealing. Stuff I used to look forward to on break kind of feels like cardboard now, or like too much effort. I don’t know exactly how much weight I’ve lost, if I have, because I don’t really check all the time, but the appetite part, yeah… that’s definitely changed.
Would you say that you’ve had a depressed mood — like feeling sad, empty, or hopeless — most of the day, nearly every day, for the past two months?

I don’t know if I’d put it exactly like that… like, “most of the day, nearly every day for two months” sounds so definite, and I’m not sure I’ve been keeping track that cleanly.

I mean, I have had a lot of days where I feel low, or kind of empty, like I’m just moving through everything without much point to it. But if you’re asking me to say it’s been every day, or nearly every day, all day long, I don’t know. Some days it’s more like it comes in waves, and other days I just feel numb more than sad. It’s hard for me to separate “sad” from just being tired of everything, if that makes sense.

So… I guess I’d say I’ve noticed feeling down a lot, but I’m not totally sure about the exact timing or whether it’s been as constant as you’re describing.
Would you say that your thoughts have been slowed down or that it’s been harder to think clearly most days, even if you’re not particularly stressed or tired?

Yeah… I think that’s been happening. It’s not like I suddenly don’t know how to do my job or anything, but I feel slower in my head.

Like at work, I’ll be doing really basic stuff I’ve done a hundred times, and I lose my place. Counting inventory is a big one. I’ll be counting shirts or boxes or whatever, and then I’ll get to, I don’t know, 23 or 24, and suddenly I’m not sure if I skipped something or counted the same stack twice. So I start over, and then I second-guess that count too. It makes something that should take two minutes take forever.

Or with displays, picking colors or deciding what should go together… I used to be able to just look at it and go, okay, this works, put that there. Now I’ll stand there looking at two options like it’s some huge decision. I’ll switch things around and then switch them back, because I can’t tell if it looks right anymore or if I’m just overthinking it.

It’s frustrating because it’s simple stuff. I’m not trying to solve some big complicated problem. It’s just normal work things, and my brain feels like it keeps catching or stalling. And then once I notice I’m doing it, I get more unsure, like, “Why can’t I just do this?” So… yeah, I’d say most days it feels harder to think clearly than it used to.
Have you noticed that you're moving more slowly than usual, or that you're restless and can't sit still, nearly every day?

I’m not really sure about that one. I don’t think I’ve noticed it in the same obvious way, like someone saying, “Why are you walking so slow?” or “Why are you fidgeting so much?” Nobody’s really pointed that out to me.

I mean, I might move slower when I’m tired or when I’m dragging through a shift, but I don’t know if it’s the kind of thing you mean, like nearly every day or noticeable to other people. And I wouldn’t say I’m constantly pacing or unable to sit still either. Sometimes I’ll shift around or feel kind of uncomfortable, but that could just be normal, I guess.

So… I don’t know. I haven’t really been tracking my body like that. If it’s happening, it hasn’t stood out to me the way some other things have.
Would you say that you've completely lost interest in things you used to enjoy, like art events or playing basketball, or do you still have some interest, even if it feels muted?

Yeah… I still have, I guess, some memory of liking those things, if that makes sense. Like I know I used to get excited about gallery nights, or going to see local art stuff, and I’d actually look forward to it during the week. Same with basketball — even just messing around, not anything serious — I used to be into it once I got there.

But lately it’s more like… I show up and I’m just kind of standing there. I’ll be at something that should be fun, like a gallery thing or grabbing tacos from a food truck with people, and I can tell everyone else is enjoying it, talking, looking around, making jokes, and I’m just sort of flat. Not mad, not exactly bored even, just like there’s nothing really reaching me.

And with helping kids with art stuff, that used to feel good to me. Like I’d get into helping them pick colors or showing them little tricks, and now I’ll be there and I’m thinking about how soon I can leave, or I’ll make some excuse like I’m tired or I’ve got something else to do. I don’t even always know if the excuse is real. It’s just… I don’t want to be there, even though part of me thinks I should want to be there.

So I don’t know if I’d say “completely” lost interest, because I still know those are things I used to care about. But actually feeling interested in the moment? That’s been really muted. A lot of times I just feel flat and end up leaving early if I can.

Would you say that your low mood and the other symptoms you've described — like losing interest in things, changes in appetite, and feeling slowed down — have occurred almost every day for at least two weeks at a time, rather than just coming and going occasionally?

Yeah… I’d say it’s been more like almost every day, not just random bad days here and there.

It’s been going on for about two months now, I think. It kind of started after that window display award at work, when the district manager started paying more attention to me. At first I thought maybe I was just thrown off by all of that, like maybe I was uncomfortable being noticed or something, and it would settle down after a few days. But it didn’t really go away.

Since then it’s been pretty constant. Some days are a little lighter than others, I guess, but it’s not like I have one bad day and then I’m back to normal for a week. It’s more like this same heaviness or flatness is just there most days, and the other stuff comes along with it. So yeah, definitely more than two weeks. Closer to two months.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t know if I would’ve described it that way before, but lately I keep getting stuck on this idea that I’m not really good enough for things people are saying I’m good enough for.

Like at work, there was this award thing, and people acted like I earned it, and I know on paper I guess I did the job or whatever, but I keep thinking… no, they must not be seeing it right. Like I don’t deserve it. And then there’s been talk about maybe giving me a chance at supervisor, and instead of feeling proud or excited, I mostly feel this guilt in my stomach, like I somehow tricked everyone into thinking I’m better than I am.

People tell me, “No, you didn’t trick anybody, you work hard,” and I try to hear that, but it doesn’t really stick. I just keep replaying it and thinking they’re going to realize they made a mistake. And then I feel bad for even being considered, like someone else should have gotten it and I’m taking up space I didn’t earn. It’s embarrassing, because I know it probably sounds like I’m fishing for reassurance, but it doesn’t feel like that. It feels like I actually did something wrong, even though I can’t point to what.

Even little things start feeling like they take way more out of me than they should. Straightening the racks, walking back to the stockroom, going to grab something for a customer… stuff I’ve done a million times without even thinking about it. Lately it’s like my legs don’t want to cooperate, or like I’m carrying extra weight around. Not pain exactly, just this drained feeling.

And I’ll catch myself standing there for a second before I go do something, not because I’m trying to be lazy, but because it feels like I have to talk myself into moving. I don’t like that. I used to be able to get through a shift and still feel like I had something left in me, but now halfway through I’m already thinking, “How am I going to get through the rest of this?”

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a significant change in sleep patterns, specifically insomnia or hypersomnia, which would support a diagnosis of major depressive disorder.
doctor.question: Have you noticed any changes in your sleep lately, like having trouble falling asleep, waking up frequently during the night, or sleeping much more or much less than usual?

target_item.name: Sleep_Disturbance
target_item.manifestation: Most nights I lie there replaying the award thing and the store conversations, then if I do fall asleep I wake up way too early and cannot get my mind to shut back off.
target_item.reason: The doctor is directly asking about changes in sleep, including trouble falling asleep, waking during the night, or sleeping more or less than usual.

patient.answer:
Yeah… sleep has been kind of messed up, I guess. Not like I’m up all night every single night, but most nights I get in bed and then my brain just starts going. It’s like the second there’s nothing else happening, I start replaying stuff from the store.

Especially the award thing. I’ll go back over what people said, how they looked when they said it, whether they really meant it, whether they were just being nice, whether I looked stupid accepting it… and then I start thinking about the supervisor conversations too, like if they’re talking about me when I’m not there, or if they’re going to realize they picked the wrong person. It just keeps looping, and I’ll tell myself, “Just stop thinking about it,” but that doesn’t really do anything.

Sometimes I do eventually fall asleep, but then I’ll wake up way too early, like before I need to be up, and once I’m awake my mind turns right back on. I can’t get it to shut back off. I’ll just lie there staring at the ceiling or checking the time and thinking, “If I fall asleep right now I can still get a little more,” but then that makes me more awake somehow. So yeah, it’s definitely not normal for me lately.

inference.note: The patient's symptoms of anhedonia, low energy, self-worth issues, and sleep disturbance align with moderate to severe depressive episode criteria. The lack of clear-cut 'down' mood most days and absence of psychomotor agitation/retardation or suicidal ideation likely rules out F32.0, F32.9, F33.0, and F33.9.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a slowing of thoughts or diminished ability to concentrate, which would support a diagnosis of major depressive disorder with psychomotor retardation or cognitive impairment.
doctor.question: Have you noticed that your thoughts feel slower than usual, or that it's harder to focus or make decisions, even about small things?

target_item.name: Diminished_Thinking
target_item.manifestation: At work I keep losing my place on simple stuff, like counting inventory or picking colors for a display, and I end up second-guessing myself over things I used to do fast.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about slower thoughts, difficulty focusing, and trouble making decisions, which directly matches diminished thinking/concentration and indecisiveness.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I think that’s been happening, actually. I didn’t really connect it to anything at first, because it sounds so small, but at work I keep losing my place on things that should be easy for me.

Like if I’m counting inventory, I’ll get halfway through a shelf or a box and then suddenly I’m not sure what number I was on, so I have to start over. And then I start getting annoyed with myself because it’s not complicated math or anything, it’s just counting, but my brain feels like it slips off the track. I’ll be standing there staring at the items, trying to remember if I counted that row already, and then I second-guess it so much that I don’t trust whatever number I came up with.

Same with setting up displays. Picking colors or deciding what should go where used to be something I could do pretty fast. I mean, maybe not perfect, but I could just make a choice and move on. Now I’ll stand there with two shirts or whatever and go back and forth like it’s some huge decision. I’ll think, “This one looks better,” and then immediately think, “No, that’s wrong, why would you pick that?” And then I waste time on it and feel stupid because it’s such a basic part of my job.

So yeah, I don’t know if my thoughts are slower exactly, but it feels harder to stay focused and harder to trust little decisions I used to make without thinking so much.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences suicidal ideation, a key symptom that helps differentiate between mild, moderate, and severe depressive episodes.
doctor.question: Have you ever felt like life isn’t worth living, or had thoughts about not wanting to be alive?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about suicidal thoughts or passive death wishes, but the provided symptom profile does not include an item covering suicidality.

patient.answer:
I… I don’t know. I mean, I don’t think I’ve had it in the way you’re asking, like where I’ve sat down and thought, “I don’t want to be alive,” or anything clear like that.

Sometimes I do get really worn down and I’ll think things like, “I can’t keep feeling like this,” but that feels more like being overwhelmed than actually wanting to die. I don’t know if that makes sense. It’s more like I want everything to stop for a while, or I want my head to quiet down, not that I’ve made some decision or plan or something.

So… no, I don’t think I’ve had thoughts about not wanting to be alive. Not really.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a persistent depressed mood most of the day, nearly every day, as required for a major depressive episode.
doctor.question: Would you say that you’ve been feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, not just occasionally or in response to specific things?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about persistently depressed mood most of the day nearly every day, but the provided symptom profile does not include a distinct Depressed_Mood item.

patient.answer:
I’m not really sure how to answer that cleanly. I mean, I wouldn’t say I’m happy or anything, but “depressed most of the day nearly every day” sounds… I don’t know, like a very specific thing, and I don’t know if I can say that for sure.

There are definitely parts of the day where I feel really low or heavy, but sometimes it feels more tied to whatever I’m thinking about at that moment, or what’s happening around me. Like if I’m busy, I might not notice it as much, and then when things get quiet it kind of comes back. So I don’t know if that counts as most of the day or not.

I guess I’ve felt off for a while, but I’m not sure I’d describe it as being down all day, every day. It’s more like it comes in waves, or it’s sitting in the background and gets louder sometimes. Does that make sense?

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a major depressive episode lasting at least two weeks, as required for diagnoses like F32.1, F32.2, F32.3, and to assess whether it may be part of a recurrent pattern (F33.x).
doctor.question: How long have you been feeling this way overall — like things feel flat, you don’t have the same interest in activities, and everything feels heavier than before?

target_item.name: Duration
target_item.manifestation: This has been going on for about two months, since the window display award and all the attention from the district manager.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking how long the overall symptoms have been going on, which directly matches the duration item.

patient.answer:
I think… overall it’s been about two months. Maybe a little hard to pin down exactly, because at first I didn’t think of it like “something started,” you know? It just felt like I was tired or stressed or maybe I was overthinking things.

But if I’m being honest, it lines up pretty close with when I got that window display award at work, and then the district manager started paying attention to me. Everyone was making a big deal about it for a while, and after that is when things started feeling different. Like the stuff that used to feel normal or even kind of enjoyable started feeling heavier, flatter, like I had to force myself through it more.

So… yeah. I’d say around two months, since all that attention happened after the display award.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a significant loss of pleasure in activities they used to enjoy, a key symptom of major depressive disorder.
doctor.question: Have you noticed that you no longer get any pleasure or satisfaction out of things you used to enjoy, like the art events or playing basketball?

target_item.name: Loss_of_Interest
target_item.manifestation: I used to get excited about gallery nights, playing basketball, grabbing food-truck tacos, or helping kids with art stuff, but lately I just stand there feeling flat and usually make an excuse to leave.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking directly about no longer getting pleasure or satisfaction from activities previously enjoyed, such as art events and basketball.

patient.answer:
Yeah… yeah, I have noticed that. I mean, I didn’t really want to call it that at first, because it sounds dramatic, like I suddenly hate everything, and it’s not exactly that. It’s more like I’ll go through the motions and I know, in my head, that I used to like it, but I’m not really feeling anything from it.

Like gallery nights, those used to be something I’d actually look forward to. I’d think about what I wanted to see, or who might be there, or I’d get ideas for my own stuff. Now if I go, I kind of just stand around looking at the walls, and everyone else seems into it, and I’m just… flat. Like I’m there but not really there. Same with basketball. I used to like playing, even just messing around, getting some energy out. Lately I’ll show up and after a few minutes I’m already thinking of some excuse to leave.

Even little stuff, like grabbing tacos from the food trucks, that used to feel like a treat, you know? Or helping kids with art things, that used to make me feel useful. Now I’ll do it and I’m just waiting for it to be over. Then I feel bad because those are things I’m supposed to enjoy, or I used to enjoy them, and I can’t really explain why they don’t hit the same.

So, yeah… I guess I don’t get much pleasure or satisfaction from those things lately. I usually just make some excuse and leave early if I can.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a significant loss of energy or increased fatigue nearly every day, which would help confirm the presence of a core symptom of depression.
doctor.question: Would you say that you've experienced a loss of energy or feel fatigued nearly every day, even when you haven’t been doing much?

target_item.name: Fatigue
target_item.manifestation: By the middle of a shift my body feels heavy, like even straightening racks or walking back to the stockroom takes more out of me than it should.
target_item.reason: The doctor is directly asking about loss of energy and feeling fatigued nearly every day.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I think so. I didn’t really notice it at first because I kept telling myself, like, everybody gets tired at work, you know? Retail is standing around, moving stuff, dealing with people, going back and forth, so I thought maybe it was just normal.

But it feels different lately. By the middle of a shift my body starts feeling really heavy, like I’m wearing wet clothes or something. Even little things that shouldn’t be a big deal — straightening racks, folding things again, walking to the stockroom to grab something — it takes more out of me than it should. I’ll catch myself sort of standing there for a second before doing it, like I have to talk myself into moving.

And it’s not always after I’ve done some huge amount of work either. Sometimes the shift hasn’t even been that busy, and I still feel drained like I’ve already worked the whole day. I don’t know if I’d say I’m collapsing or anything, but yeah, it’s there a lot. Most days at work, especially halfway through, I feel worn down in a way that doesn’t really match what I’ve actually been doing.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a significant change in appetite or weight loss related to their current symptoms.
doctor.question: Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently, like a significant decrease or increase in how much you eat or how much you weigh?

target_item.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
target_item.manifestation: What made me ask for help is I barely want to eat anymore, like I will be on my lunch break at the store staring at food I used to like and I just throw most of it away.
target_item.reason: The doctor is directly asking about recent changes in appetite or weight, including eating significantly more or less or weight change.

patient.answer:
Yeah… that’s actually one of the main things that made me think I should maybe ask for help, because I barely want to eat anymore.

Like, I’ll be on my lunch break at the store, and I’ll get something I used to like — something easy, nothing weird — and I’ll just sit there staring at it. I’ll take a few bites maybe, but it feels like I’m eating because I know I’m supposed to, not because I want it. And then most of it ends up in the trash. I’ll look at it like, “Why did I even buy this?” but then if I don’t buy anything, I also feel like I’m being stupid because I know I should eat during a shift.

It’s not like I’m trying to diet or anything. Food just doesn’t really seem appealing. Stuff I used to look forward to on break kind of feels like cardboard now, or like too much effort. I don’t know exactly how much weight I’ve lost, if I have, because I don’t really check all the time, but the appetite part, yeah… that’s definitely changed.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a depressed mood most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks, which is a key feature in differentiating major depressive disorder subtypes.
doctor.question: Would you say that you’ve had a depressed mood — like feeling sad, empty, or hopeless — most of the day, nearly every day, for the past two months?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking specifically about depressed mood (sad, empty, or hopeless most of the day nearly every day), but the provided symptom profile does not include a separate depressed mood item. The duration item only covers how long symptoms have been present, not depressed mood itself.

patient.answer:
I don’t know if I’d put it exactly like that… like, “most of the day, nearly every day for two months” sounds so definite, and I’m not sure I’ve been keeping track that cleanly.

I mean, I have had a lot of days where I feel low, or kind of empty, like I’m just moving through everything without much point to it. But if you’re asking me to say it’s been every day, or nearly every day, all day long, I don’t know. Some days it’s more like it comes in waves, and other days I just feel numb more than sad. It’s hard for me to separate “sad” from just being tired of everything, if that makes sense.

So… I guess I’d say I’ve noticed feeling down a lot, but I’m not totally sure about the exact timing or whether it’s been as constant as you’re describing.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a slowing of thought or reduced ability to think clearly nearly every day, as this is a key distinguishing symptom for severity in depressive disorders.
doctor.question: Would you say that your thoughts have been slowed down or that it’s been harder to think clearly most days, even if you’re not particularly stressed or tired?

target_item.name: Diminished_Thinking
target_item.manifestation: At work I keep losing my place on simple stuff, like counting inventory or picking colors for a display, and I end up second-guessing myself over things I used to do fast.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about slowed thoughts and difficulty thinking clearly, which directly matches diminished thinking/concentration.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I think that’s been happening. It’s not like I suddenly don’t know how to do my job or anything, but I feel slower in my head.

Like at work, I’ll be doing really basic stuff I’ve done a hundred times, and I lose my place. Counting inventory is a big one. I’ll be counting shirts or boxes or whatever, and then I’ll get to, I don’t know, 23 or 24, and suddenly I’m not sure if I skipped something or counted the same stack twice. So I start over, and then I second-guess that count too. It makes something that should take two minutes take forever.

Or with displays, picking colors or deciding what should go together… I used to be able to just look at it and go, okay, this works, put that there. Now I’ll stand there looking at two options like it’s some huge decision. I’ll switch things around and then switch them back, because I can’t tell if it looks right anymore or if I’m just overthinking it.

It’s frustrating because it’s simple stuff. I’m not trying to solve some big complicated problem. It’s just normal work things, and my brain feels like it keeps catching or stalling. And then once I notice I’m doing it, I get more unsure, like, “Why can’t I just do this?” So… yeah, I’d say most days it feels harder to think clearly than it used to.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a significant slowing of movement or physical agitation nearly every day, which would help differentiate between severity levels of depression.

patient.answer:
I’m not really sure about that one. I don’t think I’ve noticed it in the same obvious way, like someone saying, “Why are you walking so slow?” or “Why are you fidgeting so much?” Nobody’s really pointed that out to me.

I mean, I might move slower when I’m tired or when I’m dragging through a shift, but I don’t know if it’s the kind of thing you mean, like nearly every day or noticeable to other people. And I wouldn’t say I’m constantly pacing or unable to sit still either. Sometimes I’ll shift around or feel kind of uncomfortable, but that could just be normal, I guess.

So… I don’t know. I haven’t really been tracking my body like that. If it’s happening, it hasn’t stood out to me the way some other things have.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a significant loss of interest or pleasure in activities they previously enjoyed, which is a key symptom of major depressive episodes.
doctor.question: Would you say that you've completely lost interest in things you used to enjoy, like art events or playing basketball, or do you still have some interest, even if it feels muted?

target_item.name: Loss_of_Interest
target_item.manifestation: I used to get excited about gallery nights, playing basketball, grabbing food-truck tacos, or helping kids with art stuff, but lately I just stand there feeling flat and usually make an excuse to leave.
target_item.reason: The doctor is directly asking about whether interest in previously enjoyed activities like art events and basketball has been lost or muted.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I still have, I guess, some memory of liking those things, if that makes sense. Like I know I used to get excited about gallery nights, or going to see local art stuff, and I’d actually look forward to it during the week. Same with basketball — even just messing around, not anything serious — I used to be into it once I got there.

But lately it’s more like… I show up and I’m just kind of standing there. I’ll be at something that should be fun, like a gallery thing or grabbing tacos from a food truck with people, and I can tell everyone else is enjoying it, talking, looking around, making jokes, and I’m just sort of flat. Not mad, not exactly bored even, just like there’s nothing really reaching me.

And with helping kids with art stuff, that used to feel good to me. Like I’d get into helping them pick colors or showing them little tricks, and now I’ll be there and I’m thinking about how soon I can leave, or I’ll make some excuse like I’m tired or I’ve got something else to do. I don’t even always know if the excuse is real. It’s just… I don’t want to be there, even though part of me thinks I should want to be there.

So I don’t know if I’d say “completely” lost interest, because I still know those are things I used to care about. But actually feeling interested in the moment? That’s been really muted. A lot of times I just feel flat and end up leaving early if I can.

The patient continues to show no signs of psychotic features or melancholic features, keeping the list within non-psychotic, non-melancholic major depressive disorders.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a significant depressive episode lasting at least two weeks, which would support a diagnosis of major depression (F32) rather than persistent depression (F33).
doctor.question: Would you say that your low mood and the other symptoms you've described — like losing interest in things, changes in appetite, and feeling slowed down — have occurred almost every day for at least two weeks at a time, rather than just coming and going occasionally?

patient.answer:
Yeah… I’d say it’s been more like almost every day, not just random bad days here and there.

It’s been going on for about two months now, I think. It kind of started after that window display award at work, when the district manager started paying more attention to me. At first I thought maybe I was just thrown off by all of that, like maybe I was uncomfortable being noticed or something, and it would settle down after a few days. But it didn’t really go away.

It’s more like this same heaviness or flatness is just there most days, and the other stuff comes along with it. So yeah, definitely more than two weeks. Closer to two months.
